title: Vanillekipferl
summary: Austrian almond crescents, tender and short, tossed in vanilla sweetener while still warm.
steps: Mix the almond flour, hazelnut flour, ¼ cup powdered erythritol and salt. Rub in the butter, then add the egg yolk and 1 teaspoon of the vanilla and knead quickly to a smooth dough.
Heat the oven to 165 °C (325 °F) and line a baking sheet with parchment.
Roll walnut-sized pieces into 8 cm (3 in) ropes, thicker in the middle, and curve each into a crescent on the sheet.
Bake 12–14 minutes, until just golden at the tips.
Rub the remaining vanilla into the coating sweetener. Cool the crescents 5 minutes, then very gently toss them in it.
dairy_free_notes: Dairy-free butter gives a softer dough that loses its shape faster; chill the shaped crescents 15 minutes before baking.
tips: A scraped vanilla bean in the coating is traditional and worth it.

origin.history: Vanillekipferl are short nut crescents baked for Christmas in Austria, Germany and the Czech lands. The crescent shape is sometimes tied to a legend about the Ottoman siege of Vienna in 1683, but there is no evidence for that story. They became a fixture of Viennese Christmas baking once vanilla grew affordable.
